newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 8.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 8 Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo, a noted Indonesian econmist, said that Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie's plan to lower interest rates by half will ruin the country's economy.
Michel Camdessus, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), said that Indonesia and other Southeast Asian nations should reduce their current account deficits.

The chief of police in the central Java town of Bantul, near Yogyakarta, has been replaced following reports that a recent probe into the death of a journalist was unlawful. Indonesia's official human right's body has said that it does not believe the current suspect to be responsible for the murder.

Economist Sumitro Djojohadikusumo said that Indonesia has to phase out inefficiences of bribery, bureaucracy and corruption if it wants lower inflation rates. He said that leekages from inefficiencies in the Indonesian production sector could be as high as 30 percent.
